page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ads_v7 is a constrained-core, memory-optimized virtual machine built on the AMD EPYC 9V45 platform. It allocates 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with symmetric multithreading, capable of reaching speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, alongside hardware support for AVX-512 vector and cryptographic instructions. A key differentiator of this constrained-core tier is its generous memory allocation: it provides 768.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (16.0 GB per vCPU). Additionally, the instance bundles 5,669 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results validate strong compute and memory subsystem performance. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU throughput scored 3,775.28 (top 10%), while multi-core throughput achieved 89,048.42 (top 25%). Memory operations showed a cached read bandwidth of 4,989.53 GB/sec and an uncached write bandwidth of 99.65 GB/sec. The system also demonstrated top-tier single-threaded compression performance, recording 41.42 GB/sec in gzip and 18.08 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. In-memory data store performance is further highlighted by 76.45 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and a PassMark database score of 29,451.72.

The instance is structured to deliver cost efficiency for software workloads that are licensed on a per-core basis but demand high memory footprints and fast local scratch storage. By restricting the vCPU count to 48 while retaining the full 768 GB memory footprint and 5.6 TB NVMe disk array of a larger chassis, it minimizes per-core licensing overhead without starving large datasets. Workloads that fit this profile include large-scale relational database engines, in-memory databases like Redis, analytics platforms, and memory-bound batch processing systems.
